name: link_fault
description: The SPI link between U1 and U2 is cut, corrupted and restored while input is flowing. U2 must release everything it is holding within 100 ms of losing the link, and a damaged frame must produce no HID report at all - a wrong keystroke on someone's computer is worse than a missing one.
requires: U1 and U2 with the SPI1 link on a header that can be interrupted
A way to corrupt one frame in flight, such as grounding MOSI for one transfer
on_this_rig: Worth running only if SPI1 is actually interrupted between the two phases, and worth running once per interruption. U2's drop count and release time are both lifetime values - the count saturates upward and the time is whichever release happened last - so the runner subtracts the baseline and decides u2_released_within_budget only when this run caused exactly one release. No release in this run leaves it unmeasured rather than passing on a fault from before the baseline; more than one leaves it unmeasured because U2 keeps only the last time. link_recovered is decided the same way: a link that answers now is evidence of a recovery only if something took it away first. crc_counter_incremented is decided only when the counter grew, since nothing here can tell a frame nobody corrupted from one that was corrupted and not counted. no_report_from_damaged_frame and resets_are_independent need PC2 and are always unmeasured.

steps.note: handshake completes and input flows again
a bad CRC must produce nothing, not a guess
U2 keeps serving PC2 while U1 restarts
U1 keeps serving PC1 while U2 restarts

checks.u2_released_within_budget: U2 released every held key within 100 ms of the cut
checks.no_report_from_damaged_frame: no HID report followed any corrupted frame
checks.link_recovered: input flowed again after the link was restored
checks.resets_are_independent: neither reset took the other board down
